title: add vpc control plane terraform: multi-az subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, peering, route53 dns
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Add comprehensive Terraform module updates to provision a Private Control Plane VPC suitable for multi-AZ deployments. This PR adds multi-az subnet support, interface endpoints (S3, STS, ECR), configurable security groups, VPC peering support for customer networks, and optional Route53 hosted zone automation for private DNS resolution. The goal is to provide an opinionated, repeatable terraform module that installers and enterprise customers can use to provision the network surface needed by Redwood Private control plane.

Summary of changes: Added a new terraform module (terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane) with the following capabilities: multi-az public/private subnet creation, NAT gateway optionality, interface endpoints for AWS services used by the control plane, security group templates with least-privilege defaults, VPC peering resource + route propagation controls, and a route53 automation helper for creating conditional private hosted zones and zone associations. Also updated Helm chart default values to expose endpoint hostnames to the installer, added integration tests and docs, and CI plan validations.

Checklist:
- [x] Module and variables implemented (main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf)
- [x] Security groups with explicit ingress/egress rules and doc comments (security_groups.tf)
- [x] Optional interface endpoints (configurable list)
- [x] VPC peering resources + sample configuration in examples/
- [x] Route53 private-hosted-zone automation with opt-in flag
- [x] Integration test that deploys module in a mock account (tests/terraform)
- [x] Docs and quickstart example updated (docs/operating)
- [x] CI terraform plan + lint step added

Commit summary (high level):
- 9f3b7a6: initial terraform module scaffold and variables
- 7a2d1f0: add multi-az subnet & nat gateway toggles
- b4e8c12: interface endpoints implementation + endpoint policy docs
- c2d9f40: security group templates and least-privilege rules
- d5a1e7b: vpc peering resources + example config
- f1b4a22: Route53 private zone automation and ownership checks
- a8c3e55: helm values + installer wiring for endpoint discovery
- e9f0d11: integration tests and CI plan job

Files changed (high level):
- terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane/* : core terraform module (variables, outputs, resources)
- terraform/environments/prod/control-plane.tfvars : sample prod settings (multi-az true, 3 AZs)
- helm/charts/private-control-plane/values.yaml : expose dnsRoute53 and endpoint config toggles
- docs/operating/private/vpc-setup.md : operator-facing setup and migration notes
- tests/terraform/* : simple terraform apply/plan smoke test for the module
- ci/terraform-plan.yaml : add pipeline stage to validate plans for module changes

Review conversation (summary):
- Rajat: requested tightening of egress rules for control-plane SG and asked for explicit comment about why S3 endpoint uses policy X. Also asked to make Route53 creation opt-in with safer defaults.
- Ava (author): updated security_groups.tf to restrict egress to known service endpoints and added comment block explaining S3 endpoint policy, plus added the route53_enable boolean default=false in variables.tf. Pushed follow-up commit b4e8c12 -> c2d9f40 -> f1b4a22.
- Nina: asked for tests to validate that peering route table propagation doesn't overwrite customer routes; added a test fixture and documentation note.
- Jordan: ran review on Helm values and asked to keep backward-compatible defaults for existing installers; added values.yaml change that keeps previous behavior unless explicit flags are set.
- Approvals: Rajat approved after security updates, Nina approved after test added, Jordan approved after helm compatibility fix.

CI and checks: Initial CI run failed terraform fmt in one file (fixed in commit a8c3e55). Plan job executed with a mock account and returned no resources that would be created outside expected scope. Security scan (terraform-compliance) flagged overly broad SG egress in first commit, re-run passed after tightening. Final CI status: pass.

Backward compatibility and upgrade notes: Module defaults are conservative (route53_enable=false, nat_gateway=false for small installs). Existing installer workflows should not change unless operator opts into new flags. Docs include a migration section describing required steps to opt into multi-az.

Release notes:
- Added terraform module to provision Private Control Plane VPC with multi-AZ subnets, interface endpoints, SGs, peering and optional Route53 automation. Opt-in via variables: route53_enable=false by default.

Merge: Squashed and merged to main. Merge commit 9f3b7a6c4d1e2b8f0a6c3d2e1f4a5b6c7d8e9f01.

If you need a walkthrough for operator onboarding (example tfvars and helm values), see examples/private/multi-az-control-plane/README.md and ping @Ava Chen for a pairing session.
release_notes: - Added terraform module to provision Private Control Plane VPC with multi-AZ subnets, interface endpoints, SGs, peering and optional Route53 automation. Opt-in via variables: route53_enable=false by default.
notes_for_ops: Default behavior is conservative (route53 creation disabled). Operators must set route53_enable=true and provide hosted_zone_id when opting into DNS automation. Peering requires accepting VPC peering on peer account and updating route tables on peer side.
testing_summary: Added simple terraform integration test that runs terraform init/plan against a minimal config in a mocked account. Test validates that endpoints and SGs are created when enabled and that route53 is only created when route53_enable=true. CI includes lint/format/plan stages.
